methodological_rigor.justification: This is a four-center retrospective cohort of 1132 stage I NSCLC patients (2013-2021) with a clear inclusion protocol (complete resection, pN0, minimum 36-month follow-up) and appropriate exclusions (incomplete resection, multiple lung cancers). Strengths include multicenter scope, sensitivity analysis adding center and calendar year as covariates, and explicit acknowledgement of selection bias and confounding by era and platform availability. Weaknesses include the retrospective design without propensity matching, reliance on five-variable multivariable models that the authors explicitly say was constrained by sample size, and absence of adjuvant-therapy data, smoking pack-years, molecular profiling, or STAS. Statistics use Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, and Cox regression with HR/95% CI; variables entering multivariable models were chosen at p<0.10 univariate (acceptable but not pre-specified), and there is no power calculation, no proportional-hazards assumption check, no multiplicity correction, and no handling of missing data described.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is an individual multicenter retrospective cohort study, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. Clinically it reinforces two actionable prognostic signals in stage I NSCLC (pT>1a and non-lepidic adenocarcinoma subtype) and raises the possibility of considering adjuvant therapy in selected early-stage patients. However, findings largely confirm existing literature (IASLC grading, prior recurrence studies), do not provide a validated prediction tool, and the surgical-approach signal is explicitly described as model-dependent and not practice-changing.

reporting_quality.justification: The authors explicitly state STROBE was adopted (reference 12) and the manuscript covers most STROBE items: design, setting, participants, variables, statistical methods, descriptive tables, main results with HRs and CIs, limitations, and funding/ethics (IRB approval noted). Gaps include no flow diagram of patient selection, no reporting of missing data handling, incomplete reporting of eligibility during the inclusion period, and only cursory justification for variable selection. No data-sharing statement, code availability, or repository is mentioned, and supplementary Table S1 is referenced but not described, so data availability scores 1.

novelty_literature.justification: The core findings (pT>1a and non-lepidic adenocarcinoma subtype predict recurrence after surgery for stage I NSCLC) are explicitly framed as consistent with multiple prior reports including Zhao et al., Woo et al., and the IASLC grading validation work cited by the authors. The multicenter Italian cohort adds confirmatory evidence and an exploratory examination of early versus late recurrence and of surgical approach, but no new biomarker, model, or mechanism is introduced. The novelty contribution is thus incremental confirmation rather than a meaningful extension.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written, logically organized into standard IMRaD sections with a dedicated Limitations subsection, and the statistical narrative is readable. Tables 1-5 and Figures 1-2 are referenced coherently, and numerical results in the abstract match those in the body (1132 patients, 19.8% recurrence, 57-month follow-up). Minor issues include some repetition between the simple abstract and structured abstract, inconsistent counts for distant recurrence (text says 138 distant then later reports 106 distant-only plus 32 combined), and a few typos in reference formatting, but these do not impede comprehension.

key_strengths: Large multicenter cohort of 1132 consecutively treated stage I NSCLC patients with uniform inclusion criteria (complete resection, pN0, minimum 36-month follow-up)
Explicit STROBE adherence plus sensitivity analyses adding center and calendar-year covariates that appropriately attenuate the surgical-approach signal
Transparent limitations section acknowledging selection bias, era effects, platform availability, sample-size constraint on multivariable covariates, and missing STAS data
Clear, consistent reporting of HRs with 95% CIs for the primary Cox model and a cautious, literature-anchored interpretation of the open-vs-minimally-invasive finding
key_concerns: Findings are confirmatory of established prognostic signals (pT>1a and non-lepidic adenocarcinoma); no new biomarker, prediction model, or mechanism is introduced
No propensity matching, no proportional-hazards check, no multiplicity correction, no power calculation, and no explicit handling of missing data
No data or code availability statement and Supplementary Table S1 not described, limiting reproducibility
Adjuvant therapy, molecular profiling, smoking pack-years, and STAS are not captured, weakening confounding control for a recurrence-prediction question
Internal numerical inconsistency regarding distant recurrence counts (abstract lists 138 distant whereas Results section describes 106 distant-only plus 32 combined)
Multivariable model restricted to five variables due to sample-size constraints, limiting residual-confounding control in a heterogeneous multi-era multicenter dataset
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a competent but confirmatory multicenter retrospective cohort that reinforces known prognostic signals without introducing new methods or validated tools; reporting is STROBE-aligned but lacks data-sharing and some analytic safeguards, placing the work comfortably in tier 3 (Cancers / BMC Cancer / Frontiers in Oncology) with minor revisions to reconcile recurrence counts, add a data-availability statement, and clarify multivariable-model diagnostics.
